ai.description: *Sitana kalesari* reaches a snout-vent length of 45–50 mm. It is brown with a series of dark rhomboidal dorsal spots and possesses a distinctive, expansive, tricolored gular fold in adult males.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Sitana kalesari* is best distinguished by its unique, vibrant orange-red throat fan (dewlap) that lacks the dark blue or black markings typical of other *Sitana* species.
ai.habitat: *Sitana kalesari* inhabits the dry, scrubby forests and rocky terrains of the Shivalik foothills in northern India, typically found at elevations below 600 meters.
ai.behavior: *Sitana kalesari* is primarily diurnal, often observed basking on rocks or open ground to regulate its body temperature before actively foraging for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sitana kalesari* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 4–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Sitana kalesari* is endemic to the Shivalik hills of Haryana and Himachal Pradesh, typically found at elevations between 300 and 600 meters.
